newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Qld Sugar Corp sees static world price in 97.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Qld Sugar Corp sees static world price in 97.

text.p: Queensland Sugar Corporation chief executive David Rutledge said he on Monday expected world sugar prices to remain static this year against a background of surplus global stocks and increasing production.
"I see relatively static pricing of between 10 and 11 U.S. cents a pound in 1997," Rutledge told an Australian Cane Farmers Association Ltd conference.
"High world production is the evil of the current situation," he said.
Rutledge said production in India, Brazil and Thailand was increasing while China and Russia were still attempting to cope with excessive imports.
"However we (Australia) continue to expect import requirements this year from Russia and China," Rutledge said.
India's sugar policy was "out of control. They completely mismanaged their domestic requirements in 1996," he said.
While the Middle East was emerging as a raw sugar importer of Australia's production, the Thai premium market had been trending downwards for the last six to nine months.
"We've got downward pressure on our returns in those markets," Rutledge said.
